paragraphs.sourceText: The ideal companion machine would not only look, feel, and sound friendly but would also be programmed to behave in an agreeable manner. Those 26 that make interaction with other people enjoyable would be simulated as closely as possible, and the machine would 27 charming, stimulating, and easygoing. Its informal conversational style would make interaction comfortable, and yet the machine would remain slightly 28 and therefore interesting. In its first encounter it might be somewhat hesitant and unassuming, but as it came to know the user it would progress to a more 29 and intimate style. The machine would not be a passive 30 but would add its own suggestions, information, and opinions; it would sometimes 31 in developing or changing the topic and would have a personality of its own.
paragraphs.translationZh: 理想的伴侣机不仅外观、感觉和声音都很友好，而且还可以通过编程来以令人愉快的方式运行。那些使与其他人的互动变得愉快的 26 个要素将被尽可能地模拟，并且机器将 27 个迷人、刺激和随和的要素。其非正式的对话风格将使交互变得舒适，但机器仍会保持轻微的 28，因此很有趣。第一次遇到它时，它可能会有些犹豫和谦虚，但随着它逐渐了解用户，它会发展到更加 29 和亲密的风格。机器不会是一个被动的30，而是会添加自己的建议、信息和意见； 31 有时，它会发展或改变主题，并且有自己的个性。

paragraphs.sourceText: The machine would convey presence. We have all seen how a computer’s use of personal names often 32 people and leads them to treat the machine as if it were almost human. Such features are easily written into the software. By introducing 33 forcefulness and humor, the machine could be presented as a vivid and unique character.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机器会传达存在感。我们都已经看到，计算机经常使用 32 个人的名字，并导致他们对待机器就像对待人类一样。这些功能很容易写入软件中。通过引入33种力量和幽默，将机器呈现为一个生动而独特的角色。

paragraphs.sourceText: Friendships are not made in a day, and the computer would be more acceptable as a friend if it 34 the gradual changes that occur when one person is getting to know another. At an 35 time it might also express the kind of affection that stimulates attachment and intimacy.

paragraphs.sourceText: As it is, sleep is so undervalued that getting by on fewer hours has become a badge of honor. Plus, we live in a culture that 36 to the late-nighter, from 24-hour grocery stores to online shopping sites that never close. It’s no surprise, then, that more than half of American adults don’t get the 7 to 9 hours of shut-eye every night as 37 by sleep experts.

Whether or not we can catch up on sleep—on the weekend, say —is a hotly 38 topic among sleep researchers. The latest evidence suggests that while it isn’t 39 , it might help. When Liu, the UCLA sleep researcher and professor of medicine, brought 40 sleep-restricted people into the lab for a weekend of sleep during which they

logged about 10 hours per night, they showed 41 in the ability of insulin（胰岛素）to process blood sugar. That suggests that catch-up sleep may undo some but not all of the damage that sleep 42 causes, which is encouraging, given how many adults don’t get the hours they need each night. Still, Liu isn’t 43 to endorse the habit of sleeping less and making up for it later.

Sleeping pills, while helpful for some, are not 44 an effective remedy either. “A sleeping pill will 45 one area of the brain, but there’s never going to be a perfect sleeping pill, because you couldn’t really replicate（复制） the different chemicals moving in and out of different parts of the brain to go through the different stages of sleep,” says Dr. Nancy Collop, director of the Emory University Sleep Center.

paragraphs.sourceText: Climate change may be real, but it’s still not easy being green
paragraphs.translationZh: 气候变化可能是真实的，但实现绿色环保仍然不容易

paragraphs.sourceText: How do we convince our inner caveman to be greener? We ask some outstanding social scientists.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们如何说服内心的穴居人变得更环保？我们询问了一些杰出的社会科学家。

paragraphs.sourceText: A) The road to climate hell is paved with our good intentions. Politicians may tackle polluters while scientists do battle with carbon emissions. But the most pervasive problem is less obvious: our own behaviour. We get distracted before we can turn down the heating. We break our promise not to fly after hearing about a neighbour’s trip to India. Ultimately, we can’t be bothered to change our attitude. Fortunately for the planet, social science and behavioural economics may be able to do that for us.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 通往气候地狱的道路是由我们的良好意愿铺成的。政治家可能会解决污染问题，而科学家则会与碳排放作斗争。但最普遍的问题不太明显：我们自己的行为。在我们能关掉暖气之前，我们就已经分心了。在听说邻居要去印度旅行后，我们违背了不乘坐飞机的承诺。最终，我们懒得去改变我们的态度。对于地球来说幸运的是，社会科学和行为经济学也许能够为我们做到这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Despite mournful polar bears and charts showing carbon emissions soaring, most people find it hard to believe that global warming will affect them personally. Recent polls by the Pew Research Centre in Washington, DC, found that 75-80 percent of participants regarded climate change as an important issue. But respondents ranked it last on a list of priorities.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 尽管北极熊悲痛万分，图表显示碳排放量飙升，但大多数人很难相信全球变暖会影响到他们个人。华盛顿特区皮尤研究中心最近的民意调查发现，75-80% 的参与者认为气候变化是一个重要问题。但受访者将其排在优先事项列表的最后。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) This inconsistency largely stems from a feeling of powerlessness. “When we can’t actually remove the source of our fear, we tend to adapt psychologically by adopting a range of defence mechanisms,” says Tom Crompton, change strategist for the environmental organisation World Wide Fund for Nature.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 这种不一致很大程度上源于一种无力感。 “当我们无法真正消除恐惧的根源时，我们倾向于通过采取一系列防御机制来进行心理适应，”环境组织世界自然基金会的变革策略师汤姆·克朗普顿说。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Part of the fault lies with our inner caveman. Evolution has programmed humans to pay most attention to issues that will have an immediate impact. “We worry most about now because if we don’t survive for the next minute, we’re not going to be around in ten years’ time,” says Professor Elke Weber of the Centre for Research on Environmental Decisions at Columbia University in New York. If the Thames were lapping around Big Ben, Londoners would face up to the problem of emissions pretty quickly. But in practice, our brain discounts the risks —and benefits—associated with issues that lie some way ahead.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 部分错误在于我们内心的穴居人。进化使人类最关注会产生直接影响的问题。纽约哥伦比亚大学环境决策研究中心的埃尔克·韦伯教授表示：“我们现在最担心的是，如果我们不能生存下一分钟，十年后我们就无法生存。”如果泰晤士河环绕大本钟，伦敦人很快就会面临排放问题。但实际上，我们的大脑会低估与未来问题相关的风险和收益。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Matthew Rush worth, of the Department of Experimental Psychology at the University of Oxford, sees this in his lab every day. “One of the ways in which all agents seem to make decisions is that they assign a lower weighting to outcomes that are going to be further away in the future,” he says. “This is a very sensible way for an animal to make decisions in the wild and would have been very helpful for humans for thousands of years.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 牛津大学实验心理学系的马修·拉什·沃斯 (Matthew Rushworth) 每天都在他的实验室里看到这一点。 “所有代理人做出决策的方式之一似乎是，他们对未来更遥远的结果分配较低的权重，”他说。 “对于动物来说，这是一种在野外做出决定的非常明智的方式，并且对人类几千年来都非常有帮助。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Not any longer. By the time we wake up to the threat posed by climate change, it could well be too late. And if we’re not going to make rational decisions about the future, others may have to help us to do so.
paragraphs.translationZh: F）不再是了。当我们意识到气候变化带来的威胁时，很可能为时已晚。如果我们不打算对未来做出理性的决定，其他人可能必须帮助我们这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Few political libraries are without a copy of Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth and Happiness, by Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein. They argue that governments should persuade us into making better decisions 一such as saving more in our pension plans—by changing the default options. Professor Weber believes that environmental policy can make use of similar tactics. If, for example, building codes included green construction guidelines, most developers would be too lazy to challenge them.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 很少有政治图书馆没有理查德·塞勒 (Richard Thaler) 和卡斯·桑斯坦 (Cass Sunstein) 所著的《助推：改善有关健康、财富和幸福的决策》一书。他们认为，政府应该通过改变默认选项来说服我们做出更好的决定，例如在养老金计划中增加储蓄。韦伯教授认为，环境政策可以采用类似的策略。例如，如果建筑规范包括绿色建筑指南，大多数开发商将懒得挑战它们。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Defaults are certainly part of the solution. But social scientists are most concerned about crafting messages that exploit our group mentality（心态）. “We need to understand what motivates people, what it is that allows them to make change,” says Professor Neil Adger, of the Tyndall Centre for Climate Change Research in Norwich. “It is actually about what their peers think of them, what their social norms are, what is seen as desirable in society. I n other words, our inner caveman is continually looking over his shoulder to see what the rest of the tribe are up to.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 默认值当然是解决方案的一部分。但社会科学家最关心的是如何利用我们的群体心态来传达信息。诺里奇廷德尔气候变化研究中心的尼尔·阿杰教授说：“我们需要了解是什么激励人们，是什么让他们能够做出改变。” “这实际上是关于他们的同龄人对他们的看法，他们的社会规范是什么，社会上什么是理想的。换句话说，我们内心的穴居人不断地回头看看部落的其他人在做什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The passive attitude we have to climate change as individuals can be altered by counting us in —and measuring us against—our peer group. “Social norms are primitive and elemental,” says Dr. Robert Cialdini, author of Influence：The Psychology of Persuasion. “Birds flock together, fish school together, cattle herd together.. .just perceiving norms is enough to cause people to adjust their behaviour in the direction of the crowd.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 我们作为个人对气候变化所持的被动态度可以通过将我们纳入同侪群体中并与同侪群体进行衡量来改变。 “社会规范是原始而基本的，”《影响力：说服心理学》一书的作者罗伯特·西奥迪尼博士说。 “鸟儿聚集在一起，鱼群聚集在一起，牛群聚集在一起……仅仅感知规范就足以使人们朝着人群的方向调整自己的行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) These norms can take us beyond good intentions. Cialdinr conducted a study in San Diego in which coat hangers bearing messages about saving energy were hung on people’s doors. Some of the messages mentioned the environment, some financial savings, others social responsibility. But it was the ones that mentioned the actions of neighbours that drove down power use.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 这些规范可以让我们超越良好的意图。 Cialdinr 在圣地亚哥进行了一项研究，将带有节能信息的衣架挂在人们的门上。有些信息提到了环境，有些提到了经济节约，有些则提到了社会责任。但正是那些提到邻居行为的人降低了用电量。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Other studies show that simply providing the facility for people to compare their energy use with the local average is enough to cause them to modify their behaviour. The Conservatives plan to adopt this strategy by making utility companies print the average local electricity and gas usage on peopled bills.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 其他研究表明，仅仅为人们提供将其能源使用情况与当地平均水平进行比较的设施就足以促使他们改变自己的行为。保守党计划采取这一策略，让公用事业公司将当地的平均电力和天然气使用量印在居民账单上。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Social science can also teach politicians how to avoid our collective capacity for self-destructive behaviour. Environmental campaigns that tell us how many people drive SUVs unwittingly（不经意地）imply that this behaviour is widespread and thus permissible. Cialdini recommends some careful framing of the message. “Instead of normalising the undesirable behaviour, the message needs to marginalise it, for example, by stating that if even one person buys yet another SUV, it reduces our ability to be energy-independent.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 社会科学还可以教导政治家如何避免我们集体自我毁灭行为的能力。环保运动告诉我们有多少人不经意地驾驶SUV，这表明这种行为很普遍，因此是可以允许的。西奥迪尼建议对信息进行仔细的设计。 “该信息不应使不良行为正常化，而应将其边缘化，例如，表明即使一个人再购买另一辆 SUV，也会降低我们实现能源独立的能力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Tapping into how we already see ourselves is crucial. The most successful environmental strategy will marry the green message to our own sense of identity. Take your average trade union member, chances are they will be politically motivated and be used to collective action—much like Erica Gregory. A retired member of the Public and Commercial Services Union, she is setting up one of 1 100 action groups with the support of Climate Solidarity, a two-year environmental campaign aimed at trade unionists.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 利用我们已经如何看待自己是至关重要的。最成功的环境战略将绿色信息与我们自己的认同感结合起来。以普通的工会成员为例，他们很可能会出于政治动机并习惯于集体行动——就像艾丽卡·格雷戈里一样。作为公共和商业服务联盟的退休成员，她正在气候团结组织的支持下成立 1100 个行动小组之一，这是一项针对工会会员的为期两年的环保运动。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Erica is proof that a great-grandmother can help to lead the revolution if you get the psychology right—in this case, by matching her enthusiasm for the environment with a fondness for organising groups. “I think it’s a terrific idea,” she says of the campaign. “The union backing it makes members think there must be something in it. She is expecting up to 20 people at the first meeting she has called, at her local pub in the Cornish village of Polperro.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 艾丽卡证明，如果你掌握了正确的心理学，那么曾祖母可以帮助领导革命——在这种情况下，通过将她对环境的热情与组织团体的爱好相匹配。 “我认为这是一个很棒的主意，”她谈到这次活动时说道。 “工会的支持让成员们认为其中一定有什么用处。她在康沃尔波尔佩罗村的当地酒吧召开的第一次会议预计将有多达 20 人参加。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Nick Perks, project director for Climate Solidarity, believes this sort of activity is where the future of environmental action lies. “Using existing civil society structures or networks is a more effective way of creating change... and obviously trade unions are one of the biggest civil society networks in the UK,” he says. The “Love Food, Hate Waste” campaign entered into a collaboration last year with another such network—the Women’s Institute. Londoner Rachel Taylor joined the campaign with the aim of making new friends. A year on, the meetings have made lasting changes to what she throws away in her kitchen. “It’s always more of an incentive if you’re doing it with other people,” she says. “It motivates you more if
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 气候团结项目总监尼克·珀克斯 (Nick Perks) 认为，此类活动是环境行动的未来所在。 “利用现有的民间社会结构或网络是创造变革的更有效方式……显然，工会是英国最大的民间社会网络之一，”他说。 “热爱食物，讨厌浪费”运动去年与另一个此类网络——妇女研究所建立了合作。伦敦人雷切尔·泰勒 (Rachel Taylor) 加入此次活动的目的是结交新朋友。一年过去了，这些会议对她厨房里扔掉的东西产生了持久的改变。 “如果你和其他人一起做，这总是更有动力，”她说。 “如果

paragraphs.sourceText: you know that you’ve got to provide feedback to a group.” P) The power of such simple psychology in fighting climate change is attracting attention across the political establishment. In the US, the House of Representatives Science Committee has approved a bill allocating $ 10 million a year to studying energy-related behaviour. In the UK, new studies are in development and social scientists are regularly spotted in British government offices. With the help of psychologists, there is fresh hope that we might go green after all. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 你知道你必须向团队提供反馈。” P) 这种简单的心理学在应对气候变化方面的力量正在引起整个政治机构的关注。在美国，众议院科学委员会批准了一项法案，每年拨款 1000 万美元用于研究与能源相关的行为。在英国，新的研究正在进行中，社会科学家经常出现在英国政府办公室。在心理学家的帮助下，我们终于看到了走向绿色的新希望。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. When people find they are powerless to change a situation, they tend to live with it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 当人们发现自己无力改变某种情况时，他们往往会忍受这种情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. To be effective, environmental messages should be carefully framed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 为了有效，环境信息应该精心设计。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. It is the government’s responsibility to persuade people into making environment-friendly decisions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 政府有责任说服人们做出有利于环境的决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Politicians are beginning to realise the importance of enlisting psychologists, help in fighting climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 政治家们开始意识到招募心理学家帮助应对气候变化的重要性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. To find effective solutions to climate change, it is necessary to understand what motivates people to make change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 为了找到气候变化的有效解决办法，有必要了解人们做出改变的动力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. In their evolution, humans have learned to pay attention to the most urgent issues instead of long-term concerns.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 在进化过程中，人类学会了关注最紧迫的问题，而不是长期关注的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. One study shows that our neighbours’ actions are influential in changing our behaviour.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 一项研究表明，邻居的行为对改变我们的行为有影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Despite clear signs of global warming, it is not easy for most people to believe climate change will affect their own lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 尽管有明显的全球变暖迹象，但大多数人仍不容易相信气候变化会影响他们自己的生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. We should take our future into consideration in making decisions concerning climate change before it is too late.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 我们在做出有关气候变化的决策时应考虑到我们的未来，以免为时已晚。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Existing social networks can be more effective in creating change in peopled behaviour.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 现有的社交网络可以更有效地改变人们的行为。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: More than a decade ago, cognitive scientists John Bransford and Daniel Schwartz, both then at Vanderbilt University, found that what distinguished young adults from children was not the ability to retain facts or apply prior knowledge to a new situation but a quality they called “preparation for future learning.” The researchers asked fifth graders and college students to create a recovery plan to protect bald eagles from extinction. Shockingly, the two groups came up with plans of similar quality (although the college students had better spelling skills). From the standpoint of a traditional educator, this outcome indicated that schooling had failed to help students think about ecosystems and extinction, major scientific ideas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 十多年前，当时范德比尔特大学的认知科学家约翰·布兰斯福德和丹尼尔·施瓦茨发现，年轻人与儿童的区别并不在于记住事实或将现有知识应用到新情况的能力，而是他们所谓的“为未来学习做好准备”的品质。研究人员要求五年级学生和大学生制定一项恢复计划，以保护秃鹰免遭灭绝。令人震惊的是，这两个小组提出了相似质量的计划（尽管大学生的拼写能力更好）。从传统教育者的角度来看，这一结果表明学校教育未能帮助学生思考生态系统和灭绝等重大科学思想。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers decided to go deeper, however. They asked both groups to generate questions about important issues needed to create recovery plans. On this task, they found large differences. College students focused on critical issues of interdependence between eagles and their habitats（栖息地）Fifth graders tended to focus on features of individual eagles (“How big are they?” and “What do they eat?”). The college students had cultivated the ability to ask questions, the cornerstone of critical thinking. They had learned how to learn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，研究人员决定更深入地研究。他们要求两个小组就制定恢复计划所需的重要问题提出问题。在这项任务中，他们发现了很大的差异。大学生关注鹰与其栖息地之间相互依存的关键问题五年级学生倾向于关注个体鹰的特征（“它们有多大？”和“它们吃什么？”）。大学生培养了提问的能力，这是批判性思维的基石。他们已经学会了如何学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: Museums and other institutions of informal learning may be better suited to teach this skill than elementary and secondary schools. At the Exploratorium in San Francisco, we recently studied how learning to ask good questions can affect the quality of peopled scientific inquiry. We found that when we taught participants to ask “What if?” and “How can?” questions that nobody present would know the answer to and that would spark exploration, they engaged in better inquiry at the next exhibit —asking more questions, performing more experiments and making better interpretations of their results. Specifically, their questions became more comprehensive at the new exhibit. Rather than merely asking about something they wanted to try, they tended to include both cause and effect in their question. Asking juicy questions appears to be a transferable skill for deepening collaborative inquiry into the science content found in exhibits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 博物馆和其他非正式学习机构可能比中小学更适合教授这项技能。在旧金山的探索博物馆，我们最近研究了学会提出好问题如何影响大众科学探究的质量。我们发现，当我们教参与者问“如果……会怎样？”和“怎么能？”没有人提出的问题会引发探索，他们会在下一次展览中进行更好的探究——提出更多问题，进行更多实验并对结果做出更好的解释。具体来说，他们的问题在新展览中变得更加全面。他们不只是询问他们想尝试的事情，而是倾向于在问题中包含因果关系。提出有趣的问题似乎是一种可转移的技能，可以加深对展览中发现的科学内容的协作探究。

paragraphs.sourceText: This type of learning is not confined to museums or institutional settings. Informal learning environments tolerate failure better than schools. Perhaps many teachers have too little time to allow students to form and pursue their own questions and too much ground to cover in the curriculum. But people must acquire this skill somewhere. Our society depends on them being able to make critical decisions about their own medical treatment, say, or what
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种类型的学习并不局限于博物馆或机构环境。非正式学习环境比学校更能容忍失败。也许许多教师没有足够的时间让学生形成和追求自己的问题，并且课程中需要涵盖的内容太多。但人们必须在某个地方获得这种技能。我们的社会依赖于他们能够对自己的医疗或其他什么做出关键决定

paragraphs.sourceText: we must do about global energy needs and demands. For that, we have a robust informal learning system that gives no grades, takes all comers, and is available even on holidays and weekends. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们必须解决全球能源需求。为此，我们拥有一个强大的非正式学习系统，不评分，欢迎所有人，甚至在节假日和周末也可以使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: “There’s an old saying in the space world: amateurs talk about technology, professionals talk about insurance.” In an interview last year with The Economist, George Whitesides, chief executive of space-tourism firm Virgin Galactic, was placing his company in the latter category. But insurance will be cold comfort following the failure on October 31st of VSS Enterprise, resulting in the death of one pilot and the severe injury to another.
paragraphs.translationZh: “太空界有句老话：业余者谈技术，专业者谈保险。”去年接受《经济学人》采访时，太空旅游公司维珍银河首席执行官乔治·怀特塞德斯将他的公司归为后一类。但随着 10 月 31 日 VSS Enterprise 发生故障，导致一名飞行员死亡、另一名飞行员重伤，保险将不再是安慰。

paragraphs.sourceText: On top of the tragic loss of life, the accident in California will cast a long shadow over the future of space tourism, even before it has properly begun.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了悲惨的生命损失之外，加利福尼亚州的事故甚至在太空旅游正式开始之前就给太空旅游的未来蒙上了长长的阴影。

paragraphs.sourceText: The notion of space tourism took hold in 2001 with a $ 20 million flight aboard a Russian spacecraft by Dennis Tito, a millionaire engineer with an adventurous streak. Just half a dozen holiday-makers have reached orbit since then, for similarly astronomical price tags. But more recently, companies have begun to plan more affordable “suborbital” flights —briefer ventures just to the edge of spacers vast darkness. Virgin Galactic had, prior to this week’s accident, seemed closest to starting regular flights. The company has already taken deposits from around 800 would-be space tourists, including Stephen Hawking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2001 年，富有冒险精神的百万富翁工程师丹尼斯·蒂托 (Dennis Tito) 花费 2000 万美元乘坐俄罗斯宇宙飞船进行了一次太空旅行，太空旅游的概念就此深入人心。从那时起，只有六名度假者以同样天文数字的价格进入轨道。但最近，公司已经开始计划更实惠的“亚轨道”飞行——更短的冒险，只是到太空舱广阔黑暗的边缘。在本周的事故发生之前，维珍银河似乎最接近开始定期航班。该公司已经向大约 800 名潜在太空游客收取了押金，其中包括史蒂芬·霍金。

paragraphs.sourceText: After being dogged by technical delays for years, Sir Richard Branson, Virgin Galactic’s founder, had recently suggested that a SpaceShipTwo craft would carry its first paying customers as soon as February 2015. That now seems an impossible timeline. In July, a sister craft of the crashed spaceplane was reported to be about half-finished. The other half will have to wait, as authorities of America’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and National Transportation Safety Board work out what went wrong.
paragraphs.translationZh: 维珍银河创始人理查德·布兰森爵士多年来一直受到技术延误的困扰，最近建议太空船二号飞船最早将于 2015 年 2 月搭载第一批付费客户。现在看来，这是一个不可能的时间表。据报道，七月，坠毁航天飞机的姊妹飞船已完成一半左右。另一半则必须等待，美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）和国家运输安全委员会当局将找出问题所在。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the meantime，the entire space tourism industry will be on tenterhooks(坐立不安）. The 2004 Commercial Space Launch Amendments Act, intended to encourage private space vehicles and services, prohibits the transportation secretary (and thereby the FAA) from regulating the design or operation of private spacecraft, unless they have resulted in a serious or fatal
paragraphs.translationZh: 与此同时，整个太空旅游业将坐立不安。2004年的《商业太空发射修正案》旨在鼓励私人航天器和服务，禁止运输部长（以及联邦航空局）规范私人航天器的设计或操作，除非它们导致了严重或致命的事故。

paragraphs.sourceText: injury to crew or passengers. That means that the FAA could suspend Virgin Galactic’s licence to fly. It could also insist on checking private manned spacecraft as thoroughly as it does commercial aircraft. While that may make suborbital travel safer, it would add significant cost and complexity to an emerging industry that has until now operated largely as the playground of billionaires and dreamy engineers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机组人员或乘客受伤。这意味着美国联邦航空局可能会暂停维珍银河的飞行执照。它还可以坚持像检查商用飞机一样彻底检查私人载人航天器。虽然这可能会使亚轨道旅行更加安全，但它会显着增加新兴行业的成本和复杂性，而该行业迄今为止主要是亿万富翁和梦想工程师的游乐场。

paragraphs.sourceText: How Virgin Galactic, regulators and the public respond to this most recent tragedy will determine whether and how soon private space travel can transcend that playground. There is no doubt that spaceflight entails risks, and to pioneer a new mode of travel is to face those risks, and to reduce them with the benefit of hard-won experience. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 维珍银河、监管机构和公众如何应对最近的这场悲剧将决定私人太空旅行是否以及多久能够超越这个领域。毫无疑问，太空飞行会带来风险，而开创一种新的旅行方式就是要面对这些风险，并通过来之不易的经验来减少风险。
